name: Japanese · Phrases · Feelings, thanks and apologies
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.note: To friends, family, anyone younger or close.

entries.term: ありがとうございます。
entries.reading: ありがとうございます
entries.note: The default polite thanks — staff, strangers, seniors.
Textbook reply; in real life many just say いえいえ.
Apology, getting attention, and even thanks — the most used word.
Casual apology to friends and family.
Apologizing for something already done, to a senior or stranger.

entries.reading: もうしわけありません
entries.note: Serious, formal apology at work or from staff.
Reply to someone's apology or thanks.
Reassuring a friend.
Thanking someone for help — warmer than just ありがとう.

entries.term: ごめん、待たせちゃった？
entries.reading: ごめんまたせちゃった
entries.back: Sorry, did I keep you waiting?
entries.note: Arriving to meet a friend.

entries.reading: しんぱいかけてごめんね
entries.note: To family or friends after being ill or out of touch.

entries.term: さっきは言いすぎてごめん。
entries.reading: さっきはいいすぎてごめん
entries.back: Sorry I said too much earlier.
entries.note: Making up after an argument.

entries.term: 聞いてくれてありがとう。
entries.reading: きいてくれてありがとう
entries.note: After venting to a friend.

entries.term: 心配してくれてありがとうね。
entries.reading: しんぱいしてくれてありがとうね
entries.note: To a friend who checked on you.

entries.term: そう言ってくれて嬉しいよ。
entries.reading: そういってくれてうれしいよ
entries.note: Reply to a compliment or kind words.

entries.term: お気遣いありがとうございます。
entries.reading: おきづかいありがとうございます
entries.note: Polite thanks to a colleague or senior who showed care.

entries.term: ご心配をおかけしました。
entries.reading: ごしんぱいをおかけしました
entries.note: Polite version, e.g. returning to work after illness.
Formal thanks or 'excuse me', used with customers and seniors.
Relief or joy at good news.
When a worry turns out fine.
Young, casual excitement. マジで = seriously.
Said to yourself or friends at the end of the day.
To family or friends; very common.
Reacting to a friend's bad news.

entries.back: I'm so sorry to hear that.
entries.note: Polite sympathy for illness, loss or misfortune.
Telling someone close that you're frightened.

entries.reading: すこしきんちょうしてます
entries.note: Before a speech, interview or first meeting.
Testing the waters after an argument.

entries.term: ああ、なんだかイライラする！
entries.reading: ああなんだかイライラする
entries.note: Venting frustration.
After a slip-up, or when being praised.
Polite relief that someone came through an accident or disaster OK.
